exposure: manual rotation followed by direct forceps
cohort: The study included 104 sequential rotational forceps births and 208 matched manual rotation and direct forceps births from a single tertiary obstetric unit over a 21-month period (Jan 2010-Sept 2012).
finding: The use of rotational forceps was associated with a statistically significantly higher rate of vaginal birth, but also of shoulder dystocia, compared to manual rotation followed by direct forceps.
mod_finding: Rotational forceps births were associated with a significantly higher rate of shoulder dystocia compared to manual rotation and direct forceps births, but not neonatal injury.
